title: DiffScene: Diffusion-Based Safety-Critical Scenario Generation for Autonomous Vehicles

control_signal.value: Adversarial objectives (safety, functionality, constraint-based) against a target AV algorithm, plus the number of guided adversarial optimization steps N as a risk versus naturalness knob.

control_mechanism.value: At each reverse diffusion step, multi-step gradient optimization of a learned model of the safety-critical objective is applied to the denoised trajectory, followed by initial-state calibration; the diffusion model itself is goal-agnostic.

base_model.value: Goal-agnostic diffusion model trained on benign trajectories, plus a separate learned model predicting the safety-critical objective; evaluated against RL-based AV algorithms in Carla.

datasets.value: Benign dataset of 6,995 trajectories collected in Carla from RL models; 5,000 generated trajectories per scenario setting (4,000 train, 1,000 test) to train the objective model.

metrics.value: Collision Rate, Incomplete Route, Speed Satisfaction; naturalness by SSPD, Frechet, DTW, Wasserstein distance and KL on acceleration; downstream collision rate after fine-tuning.

controllability_evidence.value: Collision rate rises as optimization steps N go from 0 to 30, while SSPD and Frechet grow (a trade-off). Table 1: DiffScene collision rate 0.85 (S1), 0.87 (S2), 0.79 (S3).

stated_limitations.value: Greater optimization steps raise naturalness cost; the generator must be controlled so scenarios are not used for adversarial purposes.

notes: Packet states no technical limitations section; limits listed are drawn from trade-off discussion and conclusion. Only the naturalness constraint is explored; other combinations are left for future work (page 4).
